column1: # The table from the models to the code (AUD-5, #389; AUD-6, #409): <model> <element> <kind> <file> <function> <field> <difference> <note>,
# separated by tabs, one row for each name that a model file declares and for each message and field of the models.
#   model       the file of tests/formal that declares the element
#   element     a name that the file declares (a process, a function, a destructor, an event, a table, a constant, a
#               free name), or Process:name for a message or a field: name is a variable of the definition of Process
#   kind        process, function, constant, table, event, message (a value that goes on the wire), field (a part of one),
#               check (a test that a side makes), model (a name that stands for no code: the attacker, a phase)
#   file        the file of the code, from the root of the repository
#   function    the function of that file that builds the element, reads it or checks it (a C function with its body,
#               a Go func); several, separated by commas, when the element is in more than one place
#   field       the field of the code that holds the element: a member of a struct, a constant or a parameter that the
#               file uses; several, separated by commas
#   difference  D1 to D9 of docs/formal-model.md when the code differs from ADR-0022 or ADR-0023 here, else -
#   note        what the element is, and how the code differs from the model when it does
# .github/scripts/formal.py check reads this file on every pull request: every file exists, every function is
# defined in its file, every field is in the body of one of the functions of its row, every name of the models
# has a row, and every difference that the file cites is described in docs/formal-model.md and the other way
# round. A second reading of the table against the code is the review that AUD-5 asks for; AUD-6 corrected the rows
# that the second review of AUD-5 found wrong and added the code that it found missing.

the binding type of tls-server-end-point, the QUIC path of the build before CORE-H5: only EndPointBinding, a switch of the configuration for the test of an old node, gives it now; the negative control endpoint-cert

a QUIC client that got no certificate, and so checked no pin, has no binding, and runs an encrypted session; so does a side whose msquic gives no exporter
the empty binding of a session with none

the certificate that the server presents
the public key that the certificate carries

the same secret as the server computes it, in AcceptSecurityContext

the same on QUIC
